title: What the Work Involves
description: What an automation consultant is actually hired to decide, the three shapes an engagement takes, why most automation projects fail on the process rather than the technology, what you're accountable for once a recommendation goes live, and how to do this work on a body with variable capacity.

title: Mapping Work As It Is
description: How to trace a process as it actually runs rather than as the handbook says it runs, why the waiting between steps is usually where the time actually goes, how to draw a map a team will correct instead of nod at, and why the exceptions matter more than the happy path.

title: Getting the Truth Out of People
description: Why the people doing the work rarely volunteer the workaround that actually keeps things running, how to ask questions that produce a story instead of a summary, the specific care interviewing someone whose job might get automated requires, how to run a genuinely useful interview when a live call isn't possible, and how to keep quotes, observations and your own conclusions from blurring into each other in your notes.

title: Measuring Before You Change Anything
description: Why an ROI claim without a pre-intervention baseline is a story, not a measurement; the four numbers a baseline actually needs; how to estimate honestly when no clean data exists; who really absorbs the cost of an error; and what makes a baseline survive being questioned by someone whose job is to be skeptical of it.

title: Finding Where It Actually Hurts
description: Why the bottleneck is rarely where the complaints are, how to rank automation candidates honestly by frequency and pain rather than by who complains loudest, why a universally hated step can still be a bad automation target, how to tell a client their stated problem isn't the real one, and when the honest recommendation is to automate nothing at all.
